sources.name: Sam Fazio
sources.quote: Working at Civis Systems, I’ve seen how West Oakland businesses like ours, Oakmesh Systems, and Coastline Construction are really shaping the neighborhood. It’s not just about the jobs—it’s about the community we’re building together. People here are passionate about what they do, whether it’s urban systems intelligence or construction. There’s a sense of pride in contributing to something bigger.

sources.name: Enzo Walker
sources.quote: Honestly? Those tech firms like Oakmesh and Civis—they're changing the block faster than we can keep up. I work at Oakmesh, and half the time I'm fixing pipes in buildings that didn't exist last year. The money's there, sure, but it's not sticking around here. Guys like Elias at Civis talk about 'systems' and 'efficiency,' but ask the folks at the bus stop if they feel any of that. We're all just trying to keep the water running while the city builds over us.

sources.name: Dom Will
sources.quote: Oakmesh feels like we're building something real here - not just another tech bubble. Marcus keeps us focused on civic impact, not just profit. Civis down the street? Elias runs a tight ship, all that urban intelligence work. You see their drone fleet buzzing around sometimes. Coastline's got cranes up everywhere - hard to miss them. But it's the small crews, like our construction guys, that make the neighborhood hum.

There’s a sense of pride in contributing to something bigger.

Honestly? Those tech firms like Oakmesh and Civis—they're changing the block faster than we can keep up. I work at Oakmesh, and half the time I'm fixing pipes in buildings that didn't exist last year. The money's there, sure, but it's not sticking around here. Guys like Elias at Civis talk about 'systems' and 'efficiency,' but ask the folks at the bus stop if they feel any of that. We're all just trying to keep the water running while the city builds over us.
